LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:


<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD's top-level scope contains only static variable and array assignments — no command substitutions, eval, curl, wget, base64, or obfuscation — so sourcing it executes nothing beyond benign declarations. The `pkgver()` function runs only `git rev-list` and `git rev-parse` against the already-cloned local source tree, which is standard for `-git` packages and performs no network access or execution of untrusted payloads. The `source` array fetches the package's own declared upstream (`git+https://gitlab.com/Zesko/limine-entry-tool.git`) plus the official GraalVM JDK build artifacts from `github.com/graalvm/graalvm-ce-builds`, which are the package's legitimate build dependencies. Extracting those archives writes files to `$srcdir` but does not execute them, and `--nobuild`/`--noprepare` guarantee nothing in `prepare()`/`build()`/`package()` runs. No exfiltration, download-and-execute, or backdoor behavior occurs during this gate.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Top-level sourcing and pkgver only run benign git commands.
</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is for `limine-mkinitcpio-hook-git`, a package that installs kernels for the Limine bootloader using an upstream tool from the maintainer's GitLab repository. The file follows standard AUR packaging practices throughout.

The `source` array clones the package's own upstream repository (gitlab.com/Zesko/limine-entry-tool.git) with `sha256sums=('SKIP')`, which is required for VCS sources. Architecture-specific `source_x86_64` and `source_aarch64` arrays download GraalVM Community Edition JDK binaries from the official GraalVM GitHub releases (graalvm-ce-builds), which are used as a build dependency for compiling the Java-based tool to a native image via Gradle. These downloads are properly pinned with real SHA-256 checksums (not SKIP), verifying their integrity.

The `prepare()`, `build()`, and `package()` functions perform only standard operations: renaming the GraalVM directory, checking for javac, running `gradle clean nativeCompile`, and installing files into `$pkgdir`. No obfuscated code, base64/eval usage, unexpected network requests, exfiltration, or modifications outside `$pkgdir` are present. The `pkgver()` function uses standard git commands to derive the version, and symlinks point to `/usr/bin/limine-reset-enroll` and `/usr/bin/limine-enroll-config`, which are part of the `limine` dependency.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Standard AUR PKGBUILD, no malicious behavior detected.
</summary>
</security_assessment>
